title: Session-affinity KV mapping + staged pin-release playbook for long-context profiling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: design and execute a safe, observable staged release (pin-release) to publish per-model KV cache profiles derived from session-level sequence distributions. Outcome should: (1) enable deterministic version pinning for long-context models with session affinity, (2) expose profile metadata via the model catalog, and (3) provide a rollbackable playbook for runtime and ops teams to follow during rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Profile generator produces stable profile JSON for target models with sequence quantiles and session-affinity buckets.
2) Orchestrator can pin traffic at the model-variant level based on profile fingerprint.
3) Canary with 2% traffic shows <5% regressive token-quality delta and no >10% increase in p95 latency.
4) Console shows KV hit-rate, per-session cache warmup time, and rollout state.
5) Rollback to previous pin or disable pin completes within 2 minutes and restores baseline metrics.
work_items:
- Define session-affinity key and hashing semantics
- Implement profile generator that emits: sequence_quantiles, session_affinity_histogram, warmup_signature, pinned_model_version_candidate
- Extend model catalog API to accept 'kvcache_profile:v1' metadata
- Add orchestration API to create scheduled staged releases with fractional traffic ramps and automated metric checks
- Instrument runtime to emit session-scoped KV metrics and warmup traces
- Run synthetic and production canaries, collect delta telemetry, and publish profile release notes
progress:
2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting; agreed on session-affinity definition (user_session_id -> consistent shard hash).
2026-02-20: Profile generator prototype ready; emits sequence quantiles and warmup_signature; early unit tests green.
2026-02-26: Orchestrator API spec reviewed by infra; initial feedback: need stronger idempotency guarantees.
2026-03-03: Runtime instrumentation landed in feature branch; requires runtime flag to enable profile tracing.
2026-03-08: First internal canary (dev region) started at 0.5% traffic; observed KV hit_rate uplift but slight p95 regression on 512 token tails. Investigating kernel selection differences per pinned variant.
2026-03-10: Postmortem notes: regressions tied to mismatch in quantization profile for the pinned variant; mitigation: add quantization profile sweep before pinning for affected models.
decisions: Adopt 'session' as the affinity unit (customer_session_id or synthesized request fingerprint)
Profile schema will include 'sequence_quantiles' (10th..99th), 'affinity_buckets' (low/medium/high tail), 'warmup_signature' hash, and 'suggested_pin' metadata
Staged release schedule: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at every step
risks_mitigation: Risk: pinned variant with different quantization or kernel paths can regress quality/latency. Mitigation: preflight compatibility job that compares token-level logits on sampled traces; require 'compatibility_pass=true' before moving beyond 2% canary. Risk: long-lived pins increase cache fragmentation. Mitigation: enforce TTL and automated re-evaluation every 7 days.
qa_plan:
1) Unit tests for profile generator and fingerprint stability.
2) Integration tests: orchestrator + catalog writer + runtime flag in staging.
3) Canary in 'dev' region with synthetic traces (short/medium/long sequences) and logged token-level diffs.
4) Gradual production canary with metric gates; if any gate fails, auto rollback and Slack alert to #runtime-ops.
5) Post-release smoke: run verifier that replays 1% sampled production traffic against pinned and baseline variants and checks top-1 token match rate.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback at last successful pin state via orchestrator. Steps: 1) set rollout to previous pin id, 2) drain new variant connections, 3) invalidate affected warm caches, 4) notify stakeholders and create incident ticket if rollback triggered by health gate. Expected completion: <2 minutes for traffic switch + up to 10 minutes for cache stabilization.
